title: Unify investigate/answer pipeline into single entry command

content.title: Unify investigate/answer pipeline into single entry command
content.summary: The investigate/answer skill pipeline has three compounding bugs: two separate doorways when one is expected, no guard preventing the answer-composer from voicing un-investigated prose, and an investigator that answers only the literal claim without mechanism or edge cases. All branches resolved: unify into a single /investigate command with --out modes (default: slack voiced), delete /answer entirely, add an input guard forcing fresh investigation unless the input is schema-valid investigation-result JSON, and enable bounded expansion in the investigator (always-on, relevance-gated, every adjacent fact must carry a blob-URL citation).
decisions: answer-composer stays a pure voicer and adds zero content beyond the investigation-result. Depth lives upstream in the investigator.

/investigate always runs the investigator. Only a schema-valid investigation-result JSON may skip to voicing. Raw prose always triggers fresh investigation from the codebase. The composer never sees un-verified input.

The investigator uses bounded expansion: it answers the literal claim plus a relevance-gated set of adjacent material facts. Every adjacent fact carries a blob-URL citation. Facts that prove not useful are dropped. No bloat obligation.
/investigate is the single unified entry command with --out modes. Default output is slack-voiced. /answer skill is deleted entirely with no alias.
v1 --out modes are raw and slack only. pr and linear modes are deferred until the adapters are real and voice profiles exist.
Bounded expansion is always-on in the investigator agent. Machine callers (pr-revise, pr-code-review) also get depth. This may surface additional code review signals.
The answer-composer agent is retained as the slack voicer. Only the /answer skill file is deleted.
content.problem_statement: The investigate/answer skill pipeline has three compounding bugs: (1) two separate skills (/investigate and /answer) when the user expects one unified command that does both investigation and voicing; (2) no guard preventing the answer-composer from voicing un-investigated prose, producing unverified output that looks authoritative; (3) the investigator answers only the literal claim without mechanism, edge cases, or adjacent material facts, producing shallow answers.
content.solution: Unify /investigate as the single entry command. Add --out modes (raw | slack) with slack as the default. Delete /answer skill entirely. Add an input guard: raw prose always triggers fresh investigation; only schema-valid investigation-result JSON may skip to voicing. Enable bounded expansion in the investigator (always-on): answer the literal claim plus relevance-gated adjacent facts, each with a blob-URL citation, dropping any that prove not useful.
implementation_decisions: Delete /answer skill file. Update skill-pipeline.json, model-tiers.json, and the dispatch-tasks routing table (added in commit e736f45) to remove /answer references.
Add --out flag parsing to /investigate SKILL.md. Default: slack. Accepted values: raw, slack.
Add input guard to /investigate: detect schema-valid investigation-result JSON vs. raw prose. JSON path skips to answer-composer. Prose path always spawns fresh investigator.

Update investigator agent to implement bounded expansion: after answering the literal claim, identify a capped, relevance-gated set of adjacent material facts the asker likely needs. Investigate each. Include only those with supporting evidence and a blob-URL citation. Drop any that prove uninformative. The specific cap count is unspecified and left to implementation.
Blob-URL citation construction in investigator-code is already in place from commit 3c31398. No change needed.
answer-composer agent is retained unchanged. It is now the voicing layer called exclusively from /investigate --out slack.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Always-on bounded expansion increases investigator token usage and latency. Machine callers (pr-revise, pr-code-review) pay this cost even for narrow literal claim checks. Accepted because depth may surface additional review signals.
Deleting /answer removes a named command that may appear in user docs, bookmarks, or team instructions. No alias is intentional. Existing references will need updating.

Bounded expansion relies on the investigator's judgment about relevance. A poorly calibrated heuristic could include bloat or miss material facts. The relevance-gate (drop if not useful) is a behavioral instruction, not a structural enforcement.

tasks.summary: Added --out flag parsing to /investigate SKILL.md. Step 0 documents the flag (accepted values: raw, slack; default: slack) and strips it from args before investigation. Step 3 branches on the flag: --out raw returns investigation-result JSON directly; --out slack (default) passes the result to answer-composer for a voiced Slack reply. A bash validation script with 10 checks confirms all acceptance criteria are present in SKILL.md.

tasks.title: Add input guard to /investigate (JSON vs prose detection)
tasks.description: Add an input guard to /investigate that detects whether the input is schema-valid investigation-result JSON or raw prose. Schema-valid JSON skips fresh investigation and passes directly to the voicing layer (answer-composer for --out slack, returned directly for --out raw). Raw prose always spawns fresh investigation via the investigator. Invalid JSON that does not match the investigation-result schema is treated as prose and triggers fresh investigation. This guard prevents un-investigated prose from ever reaching the answer-composer.
acceptance_criteria: Raw prose input always triggers fresh investigation
Schema-valid investigation-result JSON input skips investigation and goes to voicing
Invalid JSON (not matching investigation-result schema) is treated as prose and triggers fresh investigation
Tests cover all three input paths: prose, valid investigation-result JSON, invalid JSON
tasks.summary: Added 'Step 1 — Input guard (JSON vs prose detection)' to /investigate SKILL.md. The guard checks whether cleaned input is schema-valid investigation-result JSON (schema_version + verdict + evidence present): if valid, it short-circuits directly to voicing (Step 4) skipping the investigator; if invalid JSON or plain prose it falls through to link detection (Step 2) and the investigator (Step 3). Existing steps renumbered. Six new structural tests added; all 19 investigate skill tests pass.

tasks.title: Update investigator agent for bounded expansion
tasks.description: Update the investigator agent to implement bounded expansion. After answering the literal claim, the investigator identifies a relevance-gated set of adjacent material facts the asker likely needs, investigates each, and includes only those with supporting evidence and a blob-URL citation (using the citation construction from commit 3c31398, unchanged). Facts that prove uninformative are dropped. The specific cap count is left to implementation judgment. This always-on behavior applies to all callers including pr-revise and pr-code-review.
acceptance_criteria: Investigator returns adjacent material facts beyond the literal claim when they are relevant
Each adjacent fact carries a blob-URL citation pointing to the supporting code location
Facts with no supporting evidence are excluded from the investigation-result
investigation-result schema remains valid with the expanded output
Blob-URL citation construction from commit 3c31398 is used without modification
Tests verify a representative claim produces expansion with citations
tasks.summary: Added bounded expansion to the investigator orchestrator: a new Step 4 identifies 2-4 relevance-gated adjacent material facts after resolving the literal claim, investigates each via leaf agents, drops facts with no evidence (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), and emits survivors with GitHub blob-URL citations in a new optional adjacent_facts field. Schema, contract doc, and agent instructions updated; 17 bash checks and 12 new Python tests verify the behavior.
